definitions.explanation: Having met someone in person and being able to recognize them. Almost always used with ある or ない to indicate whether one knows someone personally.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}とは{面識|めんしき}がない。
{面識|めんしき}のある{方|かた}に{紹介|しょうかい}された。
examples.english: I was introduced by someone I already knew.

examples.japanese: {被害者|ひがいしゃ}と{容疑者|ようぎしゃ}の{間|あいだ}には{面識|めんしき}がなかったとされている。
examples.english: It is said that the victim and the suspect did not know each other personally.

notes:
Almost always appears in the patterns {面識|めんしき}がある (to know someone personally) and {面識|めんしき}がない (to not know someone personally). Rarely used outside these fixed patterns.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {面識|めんしき}がある (to be personally acquainted with)
- {面識|めんしき}がない (to not know someone personally)
- {面識|めんしき}のある{人|ひと} (a person one knows)

USAGE NOTE:
This is a somewhat formal word frequently seen in news reports and police contexts. In casual speech, {知|し}り{合|あ}い (acquaintance) or {会|あ}ったことがある (to have met before) are more natural.
